item.description:
The Accounts service provides access to user settings and profile information.

http://sparkplatform.com/docs/api_services/my_account

General

We have two APIs: the Spark API and our RESO Web API. The Spark API is what you'll use to make account updates: it can support writes and its account data most closely resembles what's in Flexmls, since there's no translation to standard RESO Data Dictionary fields. Here are the docs for the /account service.

FBS use a "tech ID" as the system key. That is a 26-digit integer string, available as an account's "Id" field, and is unique within an MLS. This is the proper way to identify accounts. There is also a "ShortId" field, which is the member's identifier in the MLS which they may know. NB: "ShortId" is not a unique identifier for accounts. When a user changes offices, a new, pared-back account with only bare-bones data is created to house their old listings from their former office. That old account is set as inactive and not visible as soon as it's created, and it shares the same "ShortId" as the active account in the new office.

The Spark API's accounts index service requires a "UserType" filter be included:

GET https://replication.sparkapi.com/v1/accounts?_filter=UserType eq 'Member'

GET https://replication.sparkapi.com/v1/accounts?_filter=UserType eq 'Office'

By default, only active and visible members and offices are returned. To get all accounts back, you'll need to include a filter on "Visible". Here's an example of pulling all accounts:

GET https://replication.sparkapi.com/v1/accounts?_filter=UserType eq 'Member' and (Visible eq true or Visible eq false)

When you set a member inactive, you'll generally want to update the "Active" and the "Visible" field to false.

Here is the list of expansions that can be included with requests for account data. Of particular note are the "Settings" and "LoginName" expansions:

GET https://replication.sparkapi.com/v1/accounts?_filter=UserType eq 'Member'&_expand=Settings,LoginName

Some expansions have a "Single Record Only" limitation (noted in the docs), which means when you use them you either have to put a specific account's tech ID in the request path directly, or else include a "_limit=1" parameter.

POST Requests

Creating a new account is achieved by posting to the account index endpoint with JSON body data:

POST https://replication.sparkapi.com/v1/accounts

It's important to note, the OwnerId field is not applicable during the account creation process.

PUT Requests

Updating an existing account is achieved by PUTting to an account-specific request path with JSON body data:

PUT https://replication.sparkapi.com/v1/accounts/20190826160135933324000000

Your HTTP requests must have the following headers:

  • "X-SparkApi-User-Agent" set to an arbitrary string (e.g. "Tangilla")

  • "Content-Type" set to "application/json"

All body data must be valid JSON and wrapped in a "D" attribute, like this:

{
    "D": {
ACCOUNT DATA HERE
    }
}

Member names

For member accounts, don't directly modify the "Name" field. Instead, modify the "FirstName", "MiddleName", and "LastName" fields, and those will in turn populate the "Name" field.

Example POST/PUT data:

{
    "D": {
        "FirstName": "Charles",
        "MiddleName": "Alexander ",
        "LastName": "Theg"
    }
}

Phone numbers

A user can have multiple phone numbers associated with their account, e.g.:

"Phones": [
    {
        "Id": "20211028205707882518000000",
        "Name": "Office",
        "Primary": true,
        "Type": "Office",
        "Number": "098-765-4321",
        "InternationalCode": null,
        "AreaCode": "098",
        "Prefix": "765",
        "LineNumber": "4321",
        "Extension": null
    },
    {
        "Id": "20211028205707882517000000",
        "Name": "pager",
        "Primary": false,
        "Type": "Pager",
        "Number": "123-456-7890",
        "InternationalCode": null,
        "AreaCode": "123",
        "Prefix": "456",
        "LineNumber": "7890",
        "Extension": null
    }
],

  • Only one phone number at a time can be designated as the primary phone (include "Primary": true with the record). If a phone record is entered and it's the only existing phone number, it will default to primary.

  • The Spark API's /accounts/meta service will list all the valid phone "Type"s set up in Flexmls. NB: it includes "Primary" but that is a bug - do not upload records with a phone type of "Primary" as those will not come through properly in Flexmls. Instead, designate a different "Type" and include "Primary": true with your POST or PUT data.

    • "Type" field must also be unique per user.

  • Do not write directly to the "Number" field for phone records. Instead, update the constituent fields from which the "Number" field is assembled: "AreaCode", "Prefix", and "LineNumber".

  • Do not write to the "ProfileDisplay" field: it is not writable and can cause failures.

  • When adding a new phone number, you must send in all existing phone data as part of your PUT request body data. PUTing a single new phone record in will erase all other existing phone records.

Example POST/PUT data:

{
    "D": {
        "Phones": [
            {
                "Name": "Office",
                "Type": "Office",
                "Primary": true  
                "AreaCode": "907",
                "Prefix": "279",
                "LineNumber": "8235",
            }
        ]
    }
}

Emails

Accounts can have multiple email addresses associated with them:

"Emails": [
    {
        "Id": "20220303234240455293000000",
        "Name": "Primary email",
        "Primary": true,
        "Type": "Office",
        "Address": "atheg@fbsdata.com"
    },
    {
        "Id": "20220303234240455292000000",
        "Name": "Secondary email",
        "Primary": false,
        "Type": "Home",
        "Address": "api-support@fbsdata.com"
    }
],

  • Only one email at time can be designated as the primary. If a record is entered and it's the only existing email, it will default to primary.

  • All "Address" fields must be unique per user.

  • The Spark API's /accounts/meta service will list all the valid email "Type"s set up in Flexmls.

  • Do not write to the "ProfileDisplay" field: it is not writable and can cause failures.

  • When adding a new email, you must send in all existing email data as part of your PUT request body data. PUTing a single new email record in will erase all other existing emails.

Example POST/PUT data:

{
    "D": {
        "Emails": [
            {
                "Name": "Primary email",
                "Primary": true,
                "Type": "Office",
                "Address": "atheg@fbsdata.com"
            }
        ]
    }
}

Addresses

Accounts can have multiple addresses associated with them:

"Addresses": [
    {
        "Id": "20220303205746216161000000",
        "Name": "Primary work",
        "Primary": true,
        "Type": "Office",
        "Address": "1234 Cambert Rd, Sterling, CA 91332",
        "Street1": "1234 Cambert Rd",
        "Street2": null,
        "City": "Sterling",
        "Region": "CA",
        "PostalCode": "91332"
    },
    {
        "Id": "20220303210755340201000000",
        "Name": "Secondary work",
        "Primary": false,
        "Type": "Office",
        "Address": "1601 Baywood Ln, Davis, CA 95618",
        "Street1": "1601 Baywood Ln",
        "Street2": null,
        "City": "Davis",
        "Region": "CA",
        "PostalCode": "95618"
    }
],

  • Only one address at a time can be designated as primary (include "Primary": true with the record). If an address is entered and it's the only existing address, it will default to primary.

  • The Spark API's /accounts/meta service will list all the valid address "Type"s set up in Flexmls.

    • "Type" field must be unique per user.

  • Do not write directly to the "Address" field. Instead, update the constituent fields: "Street1", "Street2", "City", "Region", and "PostalCode"

  • Do not write to the "ProfileDisplay" field: it is not writable and can cause failures.

  • When adding a new address, you must send in all existing address data as part of your PUT request body data. PUTing a single new record in will erase all other existing address records.

  • If you use the same "Name" value for two addresses, it'll drop one, even if the details are different. "Name" field must be unique per user. E.g. you can't have two different addresses with "Name": "Adam's address", but you can have multiple addresses of the same type.

Example POST/PUT data:

{
    "D": {
        "Addresses": [
            {
                "Name": "Secondary work",
                "Primary": false,
                "Type": "Office",
                "Street1": "1601 Baywood Ln",
                "Street2": null,
                "City": "Davis",
                "Region": "CA",
                "PostalCode": "95618"
            }
        ]
    }
}

Websites

Accounts can have multiple websites associated with them.

"Websites": [
    {
        "Id": "20220304002746757047000000",
        "Name": "Main office website",
        "Primary": true,
        "ProfileDisplay": true,
        "Uri": "https://flexmls.com",
        "Type": "Office"
    }
],

  • Only one website can be designated as the primary. If there's only one existing website, it will default to primary.

  • The Spark API's /accounts/meta service will list all the valid website "Type"s set up in Flexmls.

  • Do not write to the "ProfileDisplay" field: it is not writable and can cause failures.

  • When adding a new website, you must send in all existing website data as part of your PUT request body data. PUTing a single new website record will erase all other existing websites.

Example POST/PUT data:

{
    "D": {
        "Websites": [
            {
                "Name": "Main office website",
                "Primary": true,
                "Uri": "https://flexmls.com",
                "Type": "Office"
            }
        ]
    }
}

Tags

The "Tags" field allows you to set the "Member Type" or "Office Type" for an account. The name is a misnomer that implies a different use, and while the Spark API will technically accept multiple tags, that's not how it's used. Accounts should always have one single tag noting the account type - no more and no less. Flexmls uses the same list of tags for both members and offices. The list of tags set up in Flexmls is available via the /accounts/meta service.

Example POST/PUT request data:

{
    "D": {
        "Tags": [
            "Designated REALTOR Participant"
        ]
    }
}

Settings

The "Settings" has contains many important account settings. Here's an example:

"Settings": {
    "Brokerload": {
        "Level": "Member",
        "PartialAccess": false,
        "AddListing": true,
        "ChangeListing": true,
        "PriceChange": true,
        "Media": true,
        "Photos": true,
        "Documents": true,
        "Videos": true,
        "VirtualTours": true,
        "StatusChange": true,
        "OpenHousesTours": true,
        "MapLocation": true,
        "Supplement": true,
        "Remarks": true,
        "Supra": true,
        "SentriLock": true
    },
    "SearchRestrictions": {
        "Associations": false,
        "MlsStatus": [
            "Active",
            "CPR Testing Coming Soon",
            "Pending",
            "Closed",
            "Rented",
            "Expired",
            "Withdrawn",
            "Cancelled",
            "Coming Soon"
        ],
        "PostalCode": null,
        "PropertyTypes": [
            "A",
            "B",
            "C",
            "D",
            "E",
            "F",
            "G",
            "H",
            "I",
            "J"
        ]
    },
    "SystemAccess": false,
    "Visible": true,
    "VirtualTourProvider": false,
    "RosterOnly": false,
    "FbsIdxCustomer": false,
    "FbsBillable": true,
    "MlsSystemAccess": true,
    "Enabled": false,
    "SuperUser": {
        "Users": []
    },
    "FlexmlsProducts": [
        "DesktopIdx",
        "MobileIdx",
        "Floplan"
    ]
},

When writing to fields in the "Settings" hash, as well as the "Active" field, you need to wrap them in a "Settings" object. Example POST/PUT data:

{
    "D": {
        "Settings": {
            "Active": true,
            "SystemAccess": true,
            "FbsBillable": true,
            "BrokerLoad": {
                "Level": "Member"
            }
        }
    }
}

  • "SystemAccess" is derived from the "Active", "Enabled", and "MlsSystemAccess" fields. All three must by set to true for "SystemAccess to also be true; otherwise, it is false.

    • "Active" can be set directly in Flexmls

    • "Enabled" comes from the "System Access" Flexmls field

    • "MlsSystemAccess" comes from the Flexmls "MLS Status" field. Whether or not this is surfaced in Flexmls is determined by an MLS preference, and not all MLSs use this field. It's enabled when there is a need to allow both MLS-level users and association-level users to turn on or off member access.

  • "FbsBillable" should usually be set to true for all non-test accounts

  • FbsBillable will default to false if it's not provided

  • If you provide a null value for "FbsBillable" that will be interpreted as a false value:

{
    "D": {
        "Settings": {
            "FbsBillable": null
        }
    }
}
  • BrokerLoad: documentation on BrokerLoad and the possible "Level" values can be found here. For general use, you will only need to set the "BrokerLoad"."Level" field. This must be wrapped in a "Settings" object:
{
    "D": {
        "Settings": {
            "Brokerload": {
                "Level": "Office"
            }
        }
    }

  • Visible will default to true if it's not provided at all, e.g. for a new account.

    • You'll get a 500 error if you try to POST or PUT a null value for Visible:
{
    "D": {
        "Settings": {
            "Visible": null
        }
    }
}

Associations

While most members belong to a single association, members can belong to multiple ones. Basic association data is returned as a matter of course with account data, but for additional association information, including which association is the primary one for a given account, include an "_expand=Association" parameter with your request:

GET https://replication.sparkapi.com/v1/accounts/20190826160135933324000000?_expand=Associations​

Portion of response:

"Associations": [
    {
        "Id": "20160202165906972207000000",
        "Name": "Fargo Association of Realtors",
        "AssociationId": "FG1",
        "Primary": true
    }
]

  • A full list of the associations set up in an MLS is available from the /accounts/meta service.

  • Only one association at a time can be designated as primary (include "Primary": true with the record). If an association is entered and it's the only one, it will default to primary.

  • When adding a new association to an account, you must send in all existing associations as part of your PUT request body data. PUTing a single new association in will erase all other existing association records.

  • Updates to associations use the association "Name" rather than "Id" or "AssociationId".

Example POST/PUT data:

{
    "D": {
        "Associations": {
            "Name": "Mid Carolina Regional MLS",
            "Primary": true
        }
    }
}

Misc

There are some fields that we allow writes to only when initially creating a new account. If you attempt to updates these fields for existing accounts, the update will either fail, or else the update will appear to work but the data will be overwritten very soon afterwards with the old data from Flexmls. Here are the some of the more important of these fields (may not be exhaustive):

  • LoginName: can be set for new account but not updated; if a PUT change succeeds, it'll revert back

  • ShortId: can be set for new account but not updated; if a PUT change succeeds, it'll revert back. Note: the Spark API currently accepts a null ShortId value, but you should always provide a ShortId when creating a new account.

  • UserType: Member, Office, or Mls

  • UserLevel: Member, Office, Mls, Company, Association

  • MlsId: this is the system key for the entire MLS system; there's no reason to ever change this

Designating an agent or broker to an office

It is essential for the agent/broker account to be a member of the office before assigning them as the Designated Agent/Broker. Failure to do so will result in the following error message:

"Validation failed: OwnerId cannot be designated as an owner of this office."

Once you have ensured the account is a member of the office, you need to include the OwnerId attribute within your request. The OwnerId needs to contain the designated agent/broker ID as it's value. Additionally, the OwnerId attribute has to be nested under the Settings attribute in order to set the designated agent/broker.

PUT request containing the office ID: https://replication.sparkapi.com/v1/accounts/20220622174123733666000000

Request Body with OwnerId belonging to the designated agent/broker:

{
    "D": {
        "Name": "Dunder Mifflin Office",
        "Settings": {
            "OwnerId": "20220622174311096119000000"
            }
    }
}

Designating a child office to a company office

To designate an office as a child office, you must include the OfficeId and CompanyId of the intended company office within the JSON body.

Include the tech ID for the child office account

https://replication.sparkapi.com/v1/accounts/20241007164529498076000000

**JSON Body

**Include the company office tech ID for the OfficeId and CompanyId fields

{
    "D": {
        "Name": "Dunder Mifflin Child Office",
        "UserType": "Office",
        "OfficeId":"20241007164529498076000000",
        "CompanyId": "20220622174123733666000000"
    }
}

Designating an agent or broker to multiple offices

A designated agent/broker can be added to multiple child offices by including the "OwnerId" field within "Settings". 

{
    "D": {
        "Name": "Dunder Mifflin Child Office",
        "UserType": "Office",
        "OfficeId": "20241007164529498076000000",
        "CompanyId": "20220622174123733666000000",
        "Settings": {
            "OwnerId": "20220622174311096119000000"
        }
    }
}

Reassign members to a new office

The Spark API supports assigning members to a new office. Previously, that was an operation that could only be done in Flexmls. Here's an example of what that looks like:

PUT https://replication.sparkapi.com/v1/accounts/20190826160135933324000000

{
    "D": {
        "OfficeId": "20090501160142129962000000"
    }
}

Assigning a member account to a new office actually creates a brand new copy of the member's account - in the old office, inactive, not in lists, and with barebones data - then the agent's old listings are assigned to it.

Teams

The "Team" hash isn't modifiable via the API, though you can get data back about teams via the Spark API. Assigning team members to team accounts and changing team leaders isn't possible via the API, and those functions, as well as designating an account a team account, need to be done via Flexmls. You can create the team account as a regular account via the API, but the last step - adding the option to the account to turn it into a team account - must be done in Flexmls.

There's an explanation of the fields in the "Team" hash in the expansions section of the accounts service docs. Here are the two accounts sub-services relating to teams:

  • All Teams

  • Accounts on a Team

Teams are just a special kind of member account (member, not office). You can get the "Team" hash back for any account by including "_expand=Team" with your request. Be aware, though, that the team expansion can only be used when accessing a single listing directly with a 26-digit ID, e.g.:

GET https://replication.sparkapi.com/v1/accounts/20210217235023409805000000

The "Team" expansion can't be used with filtered accounts searches, e.g.:

GET https://replication.sparkapi.com/v1/accounts?_filter=UserType eq 'Member' and LoginName eq 'sdaveni'&_expand=Team

Team accounts will have their "Team"."Owner" field set to true. This is not to be confused with the "Team"."LeaderId" field, which lists the ID of the user who leads the team. The team and the team leader are two separate accounts. Here's an example of the "Team" hash:

GET https://replication.sparkapi.com/v1/accounts/20210217235023409805000000?_expand=Team

Part of response:

"Team": {
    "Id": "20210217235023409805000000",
    "ResourceUri": "/v1/accounts/teams/20210217235023409805000000",
    "Owner": true,
    "LeaderId": "20190826160135933324000000"
},

request.description:
The Listing Documents service allows management and retrieval for listing documents.

http://sparkplatform.com/docs/api_services/listings/listing_documents
http://sparkplatform.com/docs/api_services/listings/history

The Listing Photos service returns data about listing photos for a specific listing to be retrieved. URIs to various photo sizes are returned rather than image files.

http://sparkplatform.com/docs/api_services/listings/photos

The Listing Videos sub-service retrieval of URIs to videos associated with a specified listing.

http://sparkplatform.com/docs/api_services/listings/videos

If you are subscribed to an MLS that participates in a datashare, this query allows you to retrieve listings from that datashare.

You can pull a list of MlsId values by using the following query - https://replication.sparkapi.com/v1/standardfields/MlsId

The Virtual Tours sub-service retrieval of URIs to virtual tours associated with a specified listing.

http://sparkplatform.com/docs/api_services/listings/virtual_tours

http://sparkplatform.com/docs/api_services/listings

Incomplete listings are drafts of listings not yet entered into the system.

http://sparkplatform.com/docs/api_services/listings/incomplete

item.name: Get Metadata

request.description:
The Accounts Metadata service describes the allowable values for searching and updating various account and profile fields, often varying by MLS. Please note, this query does not display actual listing data.

http://sparkplatform.com/docs/api_services/my_account/accounts_meta

The Photos Metadata service describes the defined Tags and Privacy values for listing photos.

Please note, this query does not display actual listing data.

http://sparkplatform.com/docs/api_services/listings/photos_meta

The Videos Metadata service describes the defined Privacy values for listing videos.

Please note, this query does not display actual listing data.

http://sparkplatform.com/docs/api_services/listings/videos_meta

The Videos Metadata service describes the defined Privacy values for listing videos.

Please note, this query does not display actual listing data.

http://sparkplatform.com/docs/api_services/listings/videos_meta

The Documents Metadata service describes the allowable values for listing documents, which varies by MLS.

Please note, this query does not display actual listing data.

http://sparkplatform.com/docs/api_services/listings/documents_meta

The Custom Fields API allows retrieval of grouped lists of supported custom fields.

Please note, this query does not display actual listing data.

http://sparkplatform.com/docs/api_services/custom_fields

Displays groups of supported custom fields.

Please note, this query does not display actual listing data.

http://sparkplatform.com/docs/api_services/custom_fields/groups

The Property Types service returns a list of possible listing property types for the current user’s MLS.

Please note, this query does not display actual listing data.

http://sparkplatform.com/docs/api_services/standard_fields

The Standard Fields API allows retrieval of a list of supported standard fields and list items. Of special note is the MlsId field, which informs which other MLSs the current user may search.

Please note, this query does not display actual listing data.

http://sparkplatform.com/docs/api_services/standard_fields

item.name: Flexmls: Listing Field List Meta Translations

request.description:
This service provides a dictionary that translates the FieldList.Value for standard and custom fields to their corresponding values in Flexmls Web.

Please note, this query does not display actual listing data.

http://sparkplatform.com/docs/api_services/flexmls/listing_meta_translations

This service exposes the relationship between standard and custom fields, specifically which custom fields a standard field is composed of, and which standard fields a custom field contributes to. It is important to distinguish this service from translations which includes only fields that directly translate in a one-to-one fashion and does not account for fields derived from many source fields.

Please note, this query does not display actual listing data.

http://sparkplatform.com/docs/api_services/flexmls/listing_meta_translations

This service provides a dictionary that translates standard and custom fields to their corresponding field data used by Flexmls Web.

Please note, this query does not display actual listing data.

http://sparkplatform.com/docs/api_services/flexmls/listing_meta_translations

This query will allow you to pull a list of MlsIds belonging to the MLSs that are allowed to pull listings from the MLS that participates in datashare."

Please note, this query does not display actual listing data.

item.description:
The Market Statistics API returns summary listing data about the market in specified geographical locations for display in a table, a graph, or other uses. Note that the data returns date fields, but the day is not significant; the data is actually for the month and year, not the day, month, and year.

Please note if you want to search by location, both LocationField and LocationValue must be supplied.

The Options parameter values are determined by the specific market stat you are drilling into.

There isn't a way to search by date.

http://sparkplatform.com/docs/api_services/market_statistics
